ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Lorraine Hansberry Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Two months of epigastric and back pain, weight loss, black stools and near-fainting in a woman of 32: examination, blood tests, and urgent upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT. Concerns: Burning, boring pain under the breastbone and through to the back for about two months, worse after meals and at night; black stools on and off for three weeks; two near-fainting spells; weight down 5 kg; An urgent care clinic put the pain down to indigestion and stress five weeks ago; she does not want it put down to stress again, and wants the cause found and told to her plainly, whatever it is; She wants to finish her play and to keep writing through whatever treatment she needs, with a clear head. [S]

tr.td: Upper endoscopy with biopsy, under sedation: no gastric or duodenal ulcer; a friable, ulcerated mass on the medial wall of the second part of the duodenum next to the major papilla, oozing slowly; four biopsies taken; hemostasis with epinephrine injection

Pancreas-protocol CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast (arterial and portal venous phases), with CT of the chest: a 3.1 cm hypoattenuating mass in the head of the pancreas invading the duodenal wall; dilated common bile duct (13 mm) and pancreatic duct (5 mm); tumor contact with about 200 degrees of the superior mesenteric vein with short-segment narrowing that can be reconstructed; no contact with the superior mesenteric artery, celiac axis or common hepatic artery; no liver, peritoneal or lung lesion; no ascites

Endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle biopsy of the pancreatic head mass (three passes with a 22-gauge biopsy needle): 3.2 cm hypoechoic mass invading the duodenum and abutting the portal confluence; no ascites; rapid on-site evaluation adequate; extra cores sent for tumor molecular profiling
ERCP in the same session with placement of a fully covered self-expanding metal stent (10 mm by 60 mm) across a distal common bile duct stricture; good drainage of bile

Pancreatic multidisciplinary tumor board (surgical oncology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, gastroenterology, radiology, pathology, palliative care, nurse navigator): borderline resectable pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (venous involvement); recommends chemotherapy before surgery with modified FOLFIRINOX, restaging, then resection if there is no progression
Advance care planning conversation, about 30 minutes
Genetic counseling before germline testing: three-generation pedigree, consent, and explanation of what a positive or negative result would mean for her and her blood relatives

Outpatient palliative care consultation, two days after the diagnosis visit: symptom review, a serious illness conversation about her hopes, worries and what matters most (her writing and a clear head), and a plan for pain, appetite and sleep alongside cancer treatment

Restaging pancreas-protocol CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast, with CT of the chest, after six cycles: pancreatic head mass smaller (2.1 cm from 3.1 cm); contact with the superior mesenteric vein reduced to about 150 degrees; no arterial contact; biliary stent in place; no liver, peritoneal or lung lesion

Open pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with segmental resection of the superior mesenteric vein and primary venous repair, and removal of the biliary stent: pathology ypT2N1 (2.3 cm residual adenocarcinoma; 2 of 18 lymph nodes involved; perineural invasion), all margins clear (R0), partial treatment response (CAP tumor regression score 2); nine days in hospital, with mild delayed gastric emptying that settled

list.item: Epigastric pain for about two months, boring through to the back and worse after meals and lying flat, with nausea, early fullness, a loss of 5 kg (8 percent of her weight), and pale, loose stools: an upper abdominal cause such as a bleeding ulcer or a pancreatic or duodenal tumor must be found. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT booked this week: resolved, confirmed [S]

Iron deficiency anemia from chronic upper gastrointestinal blood loss: black stools on and off for three weeks, two near-fainting spells, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL: active, confirmed [S]

New hyperglycemia: A1c 6.6% and random glucose 132 mg/dL in a lean woman of 32 who is losing weight; new diabetes with weight loss can be the first sign of a pancreatic cancer, so it is to be confirmed and explained, not labeled type 2: resolved, confirmed [S]

Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.1 cm, invading the duodenum, borderline resectable (tumor contact of more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, no arterial contact), no distant spread, CA 19-9 486 U/mL after biliary drainage; on EUS-guided biopsy; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose primary site the sources record differently: active, confirmed [S]
Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (pancreatogenic, type 3c): A1c 6.6% at intake and fasting glucose 141 mg/dL: active, confirmed [S]
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from obstruction of the pancreatic duct: pale, floating, loose stools after fatty meals and weight loss: active, confirmed [S]
Cancer-related pain in the upper abdomen and back, 6 out of 10, with sleep broken by it: active, confirmed [S]
Obstruction of the distal common bile duct by the tumor, relieved by a covered metal stent placed at ERCP: resolved, confirmed [S]

Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea from irinotecan, grade 2 (five to six watery stools a day above her usual), starting on day 3 of cycle 5, with low potassium and magnesium and mild dehydration; no fever, blood or neutropenia; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

Oxaliplatin peripheral neuropathy, grade 1: tingling in the fingers and toes in the cold, lasting a few days after each cycle, with mild tingling at the fingertips between cycles; no effect on writing or buttons: active, confirmed [S]

After pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with superior mesenteric vein resection: loss of the head of the pancreas, with more marked exocrine insufficiency and insulin-requiring diabetes: active, confirmed [S]

list.item: Playwright and essayist; writes at home most days and is finishing a new play, with readings and rehearsals planned; speaks at civil rights events [S]

Grew up in Chicago in a family that challenged housing segregation in court; she is alert to being dismissed in health care and wants to be told the truth plainly [S]
Never smoker; alcohol a glass of wine some evenings; no drug use [S]
Not pregnant and not trying to conceive; periods regular; uses condoms when sexually active [S]

tr.td: Medical oncology consultation within two weeks to review the endoscopy, CT and any biopsy with her and plan treatment if cancer is found

Urgent work-up of epigastric pain with weight loss, anemia and new diabetes: upper endoscopy within days, pancreas-protocol CT of the abdomen with CT of the chest, blood count, ferritin, liver tests, lipase and A1c; pantoprazole until the endoscopy; return at once for fresh black stools, fainting or yellow eyes
Intravenous iron for iron deficiency anemia from blood loss, with a blood count at each visit
Tissue and staging: EUS-guided biopsy with extra cores for molecular profiling, biliary drainage with a metal stent, CA 19-9 after the bilirubin is normal, and review at the pancreatic tumor board

Germline genetic testing with counseling for every patient with pancreatic cancer, and tumor molecular profiling (including KRAS, BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, mismatch repair, NTRK and NRG1); cascade testing offered to blood relatives only if a germline variant is found

Modified FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours) every two weeks for six cycles (three months) before surgery through a port, with pegfilgrastim, olanzapine-based antiemetic prevention that spares dexamethasone because of her diabetes, loperamide for late diarrhea, and neuropathy checks; CA 19-9 every two cycles and restaging CT after four and six cycles; hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV screening and a pregnancy test first
GL-NCCN-PANC-2026, GL-ASCO-PANC-2016, GL-ASCO-PANC-2019, GL-ASCO-ANTIEMETIC-2020, GL-ASCO-CIPN-2020, GL-ASCO-HBV-2020

Palliative care from the day of diagnosis, alongside cancer treatment: symptom control, a serious illness conversation, and planning that keeps her writing at the center; oxycodone 5 mg as needed with a bowel regimen, and EUS-guided celiac plexus neurolysis if pain becomes severe
Nutrition: dietitian review at each phase, pancrelipase with every meal and snack, small frequent meals, weight at every visit

Diabetes due to pancreatic disease: home glucose checks, A1c every three months, glucose checks before each cycle; insulin rather than oral agents if treatment is needed after surgery; dilated eye examination and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio at diagnosis

Venous thromboembolism: Khorana score recorded (3: pancreatic primary and hemoglobin below 10 g/dL); prophylactic apixaban offered once the duodenal bleeding has settled; enoxaparin for four weeks after surgery
Fertility and contraception: oncofertility counseling before chemotherapy, a pregnancy test before treatment, and effective non-estrogen contraception if she becomes sexually active during treatment
Pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with resection of the involved segment of the superior mesenteric vein after restaging shows no progression

Chemotherapy after surgery to complete about six months of treatment: six cycles of fluorouracil, leucovorin and irinotecan every two weeks, without oxaliplatin because of neuropathy; insulin glargine adjusted to home glucose readings; apixaban prophylaxis resumed during chemotherapy; surveillance afterwards with history, examination, CA 19-9 and CT every three to six months for two years
Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain explanations with written information, and support she chooses; she decides who is told and who receives each note
Endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT within one week, tissue diagnosis and biliary drainage within two weeks, and a tumor board plan within three weeks of presentation
Endoscopy in two days, CT in three, EUS biopsy and stent in one week, tumor board in nine days, consultation at two weeks
Germline genetic testing with counseling and tumor molecular profiling resulted before surgery
Germline panel negative; tumor KRAS G12D, microsatellite stable, no targetable alteration
Six cycles of modified FOLFIRINOX before surgery with no delay of more than one week
Six cycles; one dose reduction of irinotecan after diarrhea; CT shows a partial response
Resection with clear margins if restaging shows no progression
Pancreaticoduodenectomy with vein resection; margins clear (R0)
Pain 3 out of 10 or less with a clear head for writing
Pain 1 to 2 out of 10 on oxycodone 5 mg once or twice a day
Weight kept within 5 percent of the weight at diagnosis through chemotherapy, with enzyme replacement and dietitian support
Weight 54.2 kg before surgery, 2 percent below the weight at diagnosis
PHQ-9 below 10 throughout treatment, with support she chooses and palliative care alongside cancer treatment
